title: Chef and Points
source_text: Today, you finally have a chance to compete with a famous coder like Chef and prove your mettle. Chef has $n$ distinct points in 2-D plane, i.e. there are never two points with both $x$ and $y$ coordinate equal and there are no two points with the same $x$ coordinate. Consider a subset of the above $n$ points which can be arranged as a sequence $p_1, \dots, p_k$, such that $x_{p_1} < x_{p_2} < \dots < x_{p_k}$ and each point $p_i$, where $i$ is in the range between 3 and $k$ (both inclusive), lies below or on the line passing between points $p_{i-1}$ and $p_{i-2}$. Chef likes these kinds of subsets. So he wants to find the size of the largest of such subsets. Input First line of the input contains one integer $T$ - number of tests. $T$ tests follow. First line of each test contains one integer $N$ - number of points. The next $N$ lines of each test case contain integer point coordinates $x_i$, $y_i$. Output For each test case, output a single integer in a separate line corresponding to the largest subset size. Constraints - $1 \leq T, N$, sum over all $N$ over all test cases $\leq 2000$ - $1 \leq x_i, y_i \leq 10^9$ Sample Input 3 3 1 1 4 2 9 3 4 1 1 4 2 5 2 9 3 4 2 3 4 1 1 2 3 2 Sample Output 3 3 4 **Explanation case 1:** We can get the sequence (1, 1) - (4, 2) - (9, 3), where point (9, 3) lies below the line between points (1, 1) and (4, 2). **Explanation case 2:** We can get the sequence (1, 1) - (4, 2) - (9, 3). **Explanation case 3:** We can get the sequence (1, 2) - (2, 3) - (3, 2) - (4, 1).
